note: The BASE half of the promulgation boundary: what the harness scaffold writes that belongs to no single artifact. Each activated governance package ships its own ownership.json fragment for its artifact's paths; sync composes base + fragments (Plan-033, ADR-0019). Read this file; never re-decide a path's class at the call site. The prose that explains the four classes is served by this package too: `vibe-ops harness policy --name ownership --print` (Plan-040 Track 1).

classes.norm: This tooling owns it. Promulgation overwrites it, and a local edit is drift to be reconciled rather than a preference to be preserved.
classes.shaped: Two owners, permanently (Plan-031, generalised by RFC-0004): the tooling owns the parts a recorded rule names — a record's structure, which migration may restructure per a recorded note; a managed configuration's keys, each written through the module that owns it — and the repository owns everything else. Promulgation never rewrites a shaped file whole.
classes.seed: Written once when absent, never overwritten. The repository owns it from the moment it exists.
classes.repo: Never written and never read for a decision. Promulgation that would touch one of these stops and reports.

paths.why: The record lifecycles, which this tooling defines. Measured 2026-08-13 as divergent in three of three repositories checked and divergent from the shipped copy — that divergence is unreconciled drift, not per-repository preference, and it is the reason this declaration is being written.
Symlinks into .agents/rules/. Pure mechanism with no content of its own; a repository editing one has broken the bridge rather than expressed a preference.
The manual entrypoint to the gate. Wiring, not policy.
The runner that composes the fragments. A repository holding its own copy shadows the live one silently, which is the failure this class prevents.
Wiring with no check logic, resolving everything from the repository root. Measured 2026-08-13 as carrying no machine-specific path in any repository checked or in the shipped template.
Authored once against the repository it describes, then maintained by whoever works there. Overwriting it would discard the map it exists to be.

The rendered block between the `vibe-ops:lifecycles` markers is this tooling's and is refreshed on every promulgation; every other line is the repository's, permanently. It was `seed` — written once and never touched again — which measured as four distinct files across four repositories, all of them describing whatever was activated on the day they were scaffolded. The divergence outside the markers is legitimate; inside them it was staleness with nothing to correct it.
Presentation, owned by the repository from its first edit.
Formatting and exclusion preferences. Identical across repositories so far, which is not authority to overwrite the first one that diverges on purpose.

The build baseline. Scaffolded once; every dependency added afterwards belongs to the repository. The root glob is `tsconfig*.json`, matching the per-package one: it named `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.build.json` by hand and missed `tsconfig.base.json`, which the scaffold writes — so promulgation into a scaffolded repository would have stopped on a path its own scaffold had just created.
Continuous-integration wiring the repository adapts to its own jobs and runners.
A documentation skeleton whose whole purpose is to be filled in.

Placeholders that let an empty record directory survive. Once the directory has content they are deleted, and re-creating them would be noise. `.agents/skills/.gitkeep` moved out to `@entelekheia/governance-instructions`'s own fragment (Plan-040 Track 5): it belongs to a single artefact now, the instruction surface, where this base half is for paths no single package's fragment claims.

The repository's own declared configuration, in any of the three forms the cascade imports. Promulgation may create it and must never rewrite what a repository declared about itself. The `.mjs` and `.js` siblings are named because the per-destination handling consult reported them unclassified while sync never met them.

The managed layer (RFC-0004): the configuration a tool writes. The tooling owns the keys a recorded rule names — `types`, `ownership`, `harness.applied`, `harness.boundary`, `harness.agreed`, `records.dirs` — each through the module that owns it; the repository owns the file's existence and every other key, which every write preserves. Committed, read only at the repository's toplevel, and never rewritten whole: a `types` entry from `setup` survives a `sync`.

Clone-local and version-control-ignored: the operator's own layer, outranking the declared and managed ones. Promulgation never writes it; what the harness records about a repository goes to the managed file (RFC-0004).

Investigations a person wrote; no governance package serves the type, so its class stays here in the base half. The record directories that used to share this entry moved to each type's own fragment as `shaped` (Plan-031).
A repository's own gate fragments, numbered to compose alongside the built-ins. The runner is the norm's; the fragments are not.

The declared exception. It dispatches to a pipeline this tooling's norm does not own and embeds an absolute path for that reason, which is why it stays clone-local and out of version control while its neighbour does not.
The repository's code. Named explicitly so that the absence of a match is never read as permission.
